frameworks.title: Word order: SOV
frameworks.body: Urdu places the verb at the END. 'I water drink' instead of 'I drink water'.

frameworks.title: Postpositions
frameworks.body: Where English says 'to the house', Urdu says 'house to' (گھر کو).

frameworks.title: Gender matters
frameworks.body: Every noun is masculine or feminine, and verbs change to match.

frameworks.title: Honour shapes pronouns
frameworks.body: آپ formal, تم familiar, تو intimate. Use تو with a stranger and you offend.

primer.title: How Urdu is written
primer.tagline: Persian script in nastaliq — the one that slopes.

facts.label: Direction
facts.text: Right to left. Urdu uses the Persian alphabet with extra letters for sounds from Sanskrit.

facts.label: Letters join
facts.text: Letters connect and change shape. In nastaliq they also cascade DOWNWARD as they join, so a word hangs like a slope rather than sitting on a line.

facts.label: Retroflex letters
facts.text: ٹ, ڈ, ڑ are made with the tongue curled back. They are written as their plain cousins with a small ط above, and they are real, meaning-changing sounds.

facts.label: Aspirated pairs
facts.text: Many consonants have a breathy twin written with ھ after them — کھ, پھ, تھ. The puff of air changes the word.

primer.hardest: Nastaliq. The same letters you learned sitting flat suddenly stack diagonally, and word shapes stop looking like the sum of their letters. It is a matter of hours of exposure, not a different alphabet.
primer.firstWin: If you read any Arabic or Persian you already have most of the letters. And Urdu spelling maps to speech far more honestly than English does.

joining.note: These never connect to the letter AFTER them. Everything else connects on both sides.

confusables.tell: One body, five letters. Dots below, dots above, and a small ط for the retroflex. This family is where most early reading errors live.
One hook. Dot inside, three dots inside, nothing, dot above.
The small ط above makes it retroflex — tongue curled back against the roof of the mouth. Urdu does this to د and ر too.
The second stroke on top turns Kaaf into Gaaf.
